# beowulf-fitt-15 review

## Pass 1

Edited `units.json` in place by script; `t`, `ln`, `v` and `p` of all 27 units verified unchanged. Totals: 1 high, 13 medium, 17 low (31 change entries).

### Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

- 991 · n · low · "Heort is a short spelling of Heorot (as at 1017)" read as if 1017 had the short form; 1017 prints the full name. Reworded to say Klaeber prints it in full at 1017.
- 997 · n · low · Holthausen's line-end shift was said flatly to "join the bands to the hinges", an inference. Hedged ("presumably"), and said Klaeber's division is kept.
- 999 · n · low · "past of windan" for `gewand`; the verb is `gewindan`. Fixed.
- 1008 · n · low · "a formula" for `sǣl ond mǣl` asserted a formulaic status nothing in the packet supports. Now "a phrase".
- 1010 · n · low · "with no pronoun" was unclear and beside the point. Removed.
- 1011 · n · low · Unsourced background that retainers "gathered round him in return". Replaced with what the compound says.
- 1013 · i · medium · "to the benches" (plural) for `tō bence` (dative singular); "gladly" did not match l or the note's "fairly, courteously" for `fægere`. Now "to the bench" and "with good grace".
- 1013 · n · low · Added "with good grace" to the gloss of `fægere`. Removed the unsourced "Benches ran along the sides of the hall."
- 1015 · i · low · "sat" has no source (`wǣran` is "were"). Now "were stout of heart".
- 1015 · n · medium · Hrothulf/Widsith claim (nephew and uncle who kept peace) is outside the sole-source texts and unhedged. Removed; the note now says the passage gives only `māgas`.
- 1017 · n · low · "The friends are the Danes and the Geats seated together" stated as fact. Hedged ("presumably; the line does not say").
- 1018 · n · medium · "Klaeber's gloss for the compound is 'treacherous deeds'" is a claim about the glossary that cannot be checked here. Changed to "I take the compound as". The "a hearer who knew the later story of Hrothulf would catch a warning" claim is unsourced; hedged to "some readers hear a hint... this passage says nothing more".
- 1020 · n · medium · "four accusative objects" committed to `segen` and `hiltcumbor` being separate items, which is open (`hroden hiltcumbor` may restate the banner). Now says so. This also keeps the 1027 count consistent.
- 1020 · n · low · "brand... gives no subject that fits" was an overclaim. Now gives the glosses ('fire, sword') and says `bearn` supplies the giver. "most editors read hilde-" changed to "several editors" (the apparatus lists five). "found nowhere else" for `hiltcumbor` was unverifiable; replaced with an honest guess statement about `cumbor` as banner or standard.
- 1023 · n · low · "in the hall, so that all see it" went beyond the text. Now "where many can see it".
- 1024 · n · low · "The cup is the formal drink offered to the guest of honour" was unsourced. Hedged.
- 1025 · n · low · "does not make a usable word" overclaimed for MS `scotenum`. Now "gives no clear word". Removed the unsourced "received in the open, where the others could see that it was earned".
- 1027 · n · medium · Checked the 'fēower mādmas' note against 1020–1023. The things named there are the banner, the `hiltcumbor`, helmet, mail-shirt and sword. "Five" holds only if banner and `hiltcumbor` are separate and the sword counts, though the text says only that the sword was carried before Beowulf. The note stated five as fact. Rewrote it: five if separate, four if `hroden hiltcumbor` restates the banner; sword not said to be given; which four is open.
- 1030 · l · medium · "the file's leaving" singular, but `fēla` is a genitive plural and the note says "leaving of files". Now "the files' leaving".
- 1030 · i · medium · "file-worked blade, hard as showers can make it" invented a reading (and "file-worked" was off: the blade is what the files left). Now "blade left by the files, hard-tempered as if in showers", in line with the note's hedge on `scūrheard`.
- 1030 · n · low · Added `hēafodbeorge` ('head-protection') which was unparsed in the note; marked `fēla` as genitive plural; `scyldfreca` is the wearer, Beowulf by implication, not flatly Beowulf (the clause is general).
- 1035 · n · medium · Speaker of `Heht` ('eorla hlēo is Hrothgar here') stated flatly although the line names no one and the phrase meant Beowulf at 791. Hedged: most likely Hrothgar, the giver since 1020.
- 1035 · i · medium · "the roof's enclosing walls" built a guess (flagged only in the note) into the idiomatic line with an invented "roof". Now "the enclosing walls", with the note calling it a guess.
- 1035 · n · low · "eodor is a different word at 1044" contradicted fitt-06 (426) and the glossary, which treat 'fence' and 'protector' as one word used figuratively. Now says it also means 'protector, lord' at 1044, as at 426, and that the lexica may or may not split it.
- 1037 · n · low · Atmospheric closer ("a saddle set with gold and jewels... fit for a king"; jewels are not in the text). Removed.
- 1043 · n · high · Grammar label wrong: `bēga gehwæþres` called "a genitive of the thing granted"; it is a genitive depending on `onweald` ('power over each of the two'), as l and i already show. Fixed.
- 1043 · n · medium · Ing was described as "an ancestral god or hero" as fact. Hedged (not settled; ancestral figure the usual guess). "full grant" trimmed to "grant". `eodor` now tied to the 426 'fence' kenning.
- 1043 · l · medium · "protector of the Ingwine" departs from the house rendering of `eodor` (l "fence", fitt-06 426). Now "fence of the Ingwine"; i keeps "guardian".
- 1046 · l · medium · "famous prince" for `mǣre þēoden`; house l is "famed lord" (fitt-02 129, fitt-03 199, fitt-05 350). Changed.
- 1046 · i · medium · "the guardian of the heroes' hoard" turned `hordweard hæleþa` ('hoard-guard of heroes') into a different relation; "those rushes" added "those"; i now "the famed lord, the heroes' hoard-keeper, repay the onrushes of battle". Also "famous prince" to "famed lord" (house).
- 1046 · n · low · The referent of `hȳ` ('them') is not stated; added that the gifts are the nearest plural.

### Findings considered and refused

- 991 · `hreþe` as 'quickly': the note already calls it a guess and lists the apparatus; no change.
- 1002 `fremme sē þe wille` 'let him do it': subjunctive jussive checked, correct.
- 1004 'subject left unstated' / genitive class + nominative `genȳdde`: grammar sound; the speculative 'feast of life' is already flagged a guess.
- 1010 l "the feast partake": odd English but transparent and follows house l at 562/618; kept.
- 1011 "(at 943 the same word was 'woman')": the glossary itself treats `mægþ` and `mǣgþ` as one word with two senses; kept.
- 1013 l "Bowed then to the bench": matches house l at 327.
- 1013 i "the glorious company" for `blǣdāgande` ('glory-possessing'): acceptable looseness; kept.
- 1015 the `wǣra[n]` apparatus account: checked against the packet (MS þara, italic wǣ, bracket n); correct.
- 1027 i "I have never heard of many men giving another...": ambiguous reading of `gummanna fela` but follows the l and the note's parse; kept.
- 1037 l "of those, on one stood": 'on' supplied from the sense, explained in the note; kept.
- 1039 'the saddle he rode to war in': follows from `hildesetl hēahcyninges`; kept.
- 1041 i "far-famed king's fighting never flagged": the king as referent is an inference from context; the note marks the reading a guess/crux; kept.
- 1045 i "use them well" for `brūcan` ('enjoy, use'): within range; kept.
- 1046 i "nobly" for `manlīce` ('manly'): acceptable idiom; kept.
- Remembered English: nothing in the i lines matched a famous translation closely enough to rebuild beyond the 1030 and 1046 rewrites above.

## Pass 2

Fresh full pass over `units.json` (all 27 units) and `gloss.json` (every parse against its line), checking the pass-1 edits too. `t`, `ln`, `v` and `p` of all 27 units verified unchanged by script; gloss keys not renamed (one `__broaden__` key moved, see below). Every `__broaden__` entry verified by script to begin with the root glossary's entry whole plus " · ". Totals: 0 high, 6 medium, 16 low (22 change entries). Pass 1's edits introduced no new grammatical error; two of its leftovers (1020 i, 1046 i) are corrected below.

### Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

units.json
- 1011 · n · low · "at 943 the same word was ‘woman’": 943 has the form `mægþa`, rendered ‘of maidens’ (l) / ‘woman’ (i). Reworded to name the form and both renderings.
- 1013 · i · low · "went to the bench" departs from the house idiom for `Bugon þā tō bence` (fitt-05 327 i: "sat down on the bench"). Now "sat down on the bench".
- 1018 · n · low · `þenden` glossed flatly "then, at that time" although the glossary has only ‘while, as long as’, and "some readers hear a hint of later trouble" is unsourced criticism. Now: usually ‘while’, taken here as ‘then / while this lasted’; the hint sentence removed.
- 1020 · i · medium · "hilt-standard" is not English a person would say (it is the l compound carried over, and the note calls it a guess). i now "an adorned standard"; note says the idiomatic line leaves out the doubtful ‘hilt-’.
- 1020 · n · low · Added the sentence just described.
- 1030 · n · low · `wala` ‘ridge’ was given as fact in the note while the gloss calls it a guess. Note now says the rare word's sense is a guess from context.
- 1039 · n · low · "The king gives away the saddle he rode to war in, a gift from his own person" asserted a gift the text does not state (the horses are given at 1043; the saddle stands on one of them). Now says the saddle presumably passes with its horse.
- 1046 · i · medium · "with horses and treasures that no man … will ever find fault with them" reads as a relative clause with a stray "them". Comma added so the `swā … lŷhð` result clause reads as such.

gloss.json
- wǣran · medium · said the MS has "wǣra" (packet: MS `þara`) and labelled the form "preterite subjunctive", which nothing supports (the clause is indicative; `wǣran` is a variant of `wǣron`). Now "3rd plural preterite; Klaeber's emendation of the MS þara".
- þe (`__broaden__`) → þē · medium · the "when" reading belongs to the form at 1000, which is `þē` (macron), not `þe`; the broadening sat on the wrong key and stated "when" as an established sense. Removed the `þe` broaden (it only added a misplaced reading) and added the old `þē` entry whole + " · þe — when, after (… a guess)". This is the one change to the set of `__broaden__` keys.
- hāten (`__broaden__`, new) · medium · existing entry has only ‘called, named’; 991 uses it for ‘ordered’. Broadened.
- þenden (`__broaden__`, new) · medium · existing entry has only ‘while, as long as’; 1019 is taken as ‘then / at that time’ (note and l/i). Broadened.
- eoderas · low · "stall" an invented sense; "the sense here is uncertain" pinned to a line. Now ‘enclosure, fence’, with the crux said in the phrase.
- hiltcumbor · low · "in apposition to segen" asserted what the note says is open; `cumbor = cumbol` unhedged. Now ‘probably a variant of cumbol’, no apposition claim.
- fēla · low · lemma and gender doubtful (masculine unverified). Lemma ‘fēol (fēl)’, gender dropped.
- ansund · low · "an- ‘one, whole’" is an unsupported etymology. Now ‘ān- + sund’.
- fyrendǣdum · low · "of cause" disagreed with the note's "of means". Now "instrumental".
- ingwina · low · "Ing being a legendary ancestor" stated as settled; note says not settled. Now ‘an ancestral figure, not otherwise explained’.
- īrẹnbendum · low · "feminine" for `bend` unverified. Gender dropped.
- hēafodbeorge · low · "feminine" unverified. Gender dropped.
- eal (`__broaden__`) · low · last added reading (‘nominative singular neuter, agreeing with bold’) duplicates the old first reading. Removed; the adverb reading for `eal inneweard` stays.
- heort (`__broaden__`) · low · new reading pinned to the clause with a speculative alternative. Now "nominative or accusative" with the example phrase.

### Findings considered and refused

- 991 `hreþe`, `hāten`, `gefrætwod` grammar: ‘was ordered … adorned’ is a fair parse; the note states the crux. No change.
- 999 `þē` ‘when’: l, i and note agree and the guess is flagged; apparatus quoted correctly.
- 1004 subject-less `gesēcan sceal` with genitive plurals: sound; note kept.
- 1015 `wǣra[n]` note, apparatus account (MS `þara`, italic `wǣ`, bracket `n`): re-checked against the packet; correct. "the formula used in Fitt XI": `sele þām hēan` at 713 (and 919); kept.
- 1017 "presumably the Danes and the Geats": hedged; kept.
- 1020 `bearn` known entry says "in apposition to a name": the form here is the subject, but case, number and sense are the same; no broadening.
- 1020 `hilt-` as ‘hilt’: Klaeber's reading; the l keeps it, the note flags the guess.
- 1035 i "cheek-pieces" and "the enclosing walls": both guesses are named in the note; kept.
- 1041 i "king": inference from context, note marks the crux; kept.
- `hrōþulf` gloss "son of Halga": the packet is silent, but names take identity (conventions) and the root glossary has Hālga as Healfdene's third son, so "nephew" is consistent; the unhedged claim was removed from the note by pass 1 and stays out of it.
- `gang` ‘went’ (preterite indicative): standard; `gēong` at 925 verified in the source.
- `niþða` lemma `niþþas`: uncertain as the glosser says; meaning and case are right for ‘niþða bearna’.
- `lŷhð` / `lēan`: parse is hedged and Sievers's alternatives are in the note; kept.
- Remembered English: none of the i lines echoes a famous translation beyond the 1046 and 1030 rewrites already made.
- All other novel and known forms checked against their lines (case, number, tense, homograph); no further error.
